**One more thing the compiler's own prelude says.** `CompilerBuiltin.fss:1483` and `:1521` carry
the interpreter library's extends clauses **commented out** —
`(*) extends { Equality[\Comparison\] }` and
`(*) extends { Comparison, StandardTotalOrder[\TotalComparison\] }`, replaced by
`extends { Comparison }` — while keeping the two `comprises` clauses that
`FortressLibrary.fsi:102` and `:122` also have. Those are four of the 27 sites
(`.fsi:121` and the three objects at `:132`, `:143`, `:153`), and the compiler prelude passes
the checker with 0 errors (`09a-spec-selfinst-asprinted.out`, `checkApi CompilerBuiltin ->
errors=0`). So the compiler world does not avoid this by dropping `comprises` — it keeps both
clauses — but by **flattening the tower** so that no self-parameterised trait is inherited
twice. `MinP.fss` is the counterfactual: put a second instantiation back into a hierarchy in
that same world and the four errors appear. The lines are present in the
tree at the parentless import root `5a68404fd` (2012-07-19) and no commit message in the
available history explains them.

well-formedness checks, whose rule the specification states in a `\note{}`

# Rung P (rung-exclusion-relax): the judge's ruling — stop, with the fork sharpened

Decision: **stop**. The worker's stop is right in substance and half wrong in its framing. The rung cannot land the relaxation alone, the closure it needs is the decision the batch record itself reserved to Pavol (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:18`, "35 the specification's sentence on differing static parameters, which is Pavol's decision"; `explorations/perf-probes/nat/triage.md:113`), and the record's own stop clause for this rung names the case (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:85`, "the fix for that is a second design decision"). What reaches Pavol is narrower than the worker's two-way choice, and section 6 states it with costs measured in this ruling.

Nothing was built or run for this ruling. It rests on the branch's net change (`git diff d610695c0...9066c6d18`: two files under `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`, the rest under `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-relax/`; nothing under `ProjectFortress/src`), the worker's REPORT.md and record.md, the probes and captures on the branch, the specification passages read with their surroundings, and the precedents at the cited lines.

## 1. What the specification settles, and how

The specification is not silent. It speaks on both halves of the problem, and its two halves form one coherent design.

**(H) A type may extend two instantiations of one generic.** `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:184-189`: the subtype and exclusion relations "are the smallest ones that satisfy all the properties given in those sections (and this one)", and the properties that make trait types exclude are an `excludes` clause (`:212-214`), arrow, tuple, `()` and `BottomType` (`:215-216`), object-ness (`:222-224`) and propagation to subtypes (`:163-164`). None concerns two instantiations. The worker cited this and it is right. The worker cited `trait-parameters.tex:339-351` as text and conceded it is the covariant case that Naden's refinement permits (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:536-537`). It missed the two passages that are decisive and invariant:

- `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:359-367`: `trait C extends D[\T\] where {T extends Object}` — "In this declaration, trait C is a subtrait of *every* instantiation of parametric trait D. Thus, trait C has all of the methods of every instantiation of D." Under multiple instantiation exclusion, "any type which is a subtype of two distinct instantiations of a single generic type is equivalent to Bottom" (`justificationOfRTR.tex:345-347`), so `C` would be uninhabited; the specification instead discusses the inference restrictions `C` needs (`:367-379`), which only a live type needs.
- `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:383-397`: `object Empty extends List[\T\] where {T extends Object}` — a single value that is a member of every instantiation of `List`. This is `BadList` (`justificationOfRTR.tex:89-98`) written on purpose, as the specification's canonical empty list. Note that its `first()` and `rest()` throw (`:392-393`): the specification's own example never produces a `T`, which is why it is sound in the specification's world.

So on (H) the specification settles it against the compiled checker's `checkP` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:443-456`) and against the two hierarchy questions that enforce it (`scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:178`, `:187`). The worker's four errors on the MinP shape (`probes/test-preedit.txt:2-10`) are that enforcement.

**(O) Overloaded declarations share their static parameters, and a call site instantiates them once.** `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-108`: "it is an error for their static parameters to differ (up to α-equivalence), or for one declaration to have static parameters and another to not have them. Hence, static parameters do not enter into the determination of which declarations are applicable". With `trait-parameters.tex:374-379` ("It must be possible to infer which method is referred to at the call site ... type checking rejects the program" otherwise), this is the specification's dispatch model: static arguments are fixed at the call site by inference, every overload of the name is instantiated at those arguments, and dispatch chooses among declarations that all carry the same instantiation. In that model `Empty` is harmless: no overload of a name can be applicable to it at an instantiation other than the caller's, because no overload has an instantiation of its own.

**The two worlds.** The specification's world: (H) allowed, (O) enforced, call-site instantiation; no need for multiple instantiation exclusion. The 2011–2012 design's world: specialised generic overloads wanted (`tail[\X\]` beside `tail`, `justificationOfRTR.tex:76-84`), which (O) forbids outright; run-time instantiation for dispatch (`Papers/RuntimeInstantiation`, the title itself); and multiple instantiation exclusion adopted to make that sound (`Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152`; `justificationOfRTR.tex:457-459`, `:476-478`, `:496-497`). Each world is coherent. The compiled checker implements the second (the worker showed this, correctly). The interpreter is on the specification's side of (H) (`interpreter/evaluator/types/FType.java:197-297`, no instantiation clause) and has its own rule on the overload side (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:496-498`). Rung P as briefed — the interpreter's (H) with the compiler's run-time-instantiated specialised overloads — is the one combination that belongs to neither world, and the worker's `probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss` is the program that shows it: links under every placement and dies with `IncompatibleClassChangeError` (`probes/probe-matrix.txt:64-68`, `:86-90`, `:108-112`). That measurement is right and it is the load-bearing fact of this rung.

## 2. Where the worker was right

- `checkP` is the designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion", by name and by rationale: `exclusion.tick:141-152` (read at `:125-165`); `justificationOfRTR.tex:76-98`, `:342-347`, `:457-459`, `:476-478`, `:496-497` (read with their surroundings). The batch record, the trace and the triage do not cite either source; the record's "designers' survey" is `explorations/run-c4/cold-cache/operators/D/SURVEY.md:46`, a revival-era note about the interpreter. All correct.
- The Return Type Rule check solves for one instantiation of the less specific declaration and trusts it: `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105`, `subEDsolution` at `:88`, the substituted return type at `:95`. Correct, and it is exactly the reliance Naden's proof names (`:449-459`).
- Relaxing `checkP` alone is unsound under every placement, and the control without the multiply-instantiated type runs correctly everywhere (`probe-matrix.txt:18-21`, `:60-63`, `:82-85`, `:104-107`). Correct; the captures were read.
- The record's call-site list misses the `typecase` redundancy checks (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:268`, `:274`, `:280`, `:332`) and the meets of `normConjunct` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:632-640`), and only the broad placement reaches them (`probe-matrix.txt:69-77`, `:91-99`, `:113-116`). Correct.
- The overloading half of the record's placement refuses row 97's shape, which the compiled path accepts and runs today (`probes/probe-overload.txt:2-6` against `:12-19`, `:24-31`). Correct, and this cost was not in the record.
- The compiler prelude's commented-out `extends` clauses (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:1483`, `:1521`) are the compiled world staying inside the rule. A sound reading of lines the trace could not explain (`explorations/perf-probes/prelude/exclusion-trace.md:167-180`).
- The expected-failure test `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExclusionRelaxRungP.fss` and `.test` is the right home-2 artifact for (H): it asserts the specification's program, fails today, and was shown red on the deliberate local fix (`probes/xxx-tripwire.txt:17-21`, `:26-43`, `:48-61`). The mechanism is `FileTests.java:384-404` (the `shouldFail` branch of `SourceFileTest`: a failure with `link_err_contains` satisfied is "Saw expected failure"; a successful link leaves `link_err_contains` unsatisfied, so `trueFailure` is set and the test is red as "Saw wrong failure"). It stays on the branch; whichever rung lands the relaxation converts it to the positive test the record asked for.

## 3. Where the worker was wrong or incomplete

1. **"Keep multiple instantiation exclusion on the compiled path" is not a live candidate**, and the worker presented it as one of Pavol's two choices (REPORT.md, "The stop", option 1; record.md, "The question for Pavol"). It is refused by the specification at `trait-parameters.tex:359-367` and `:383-397` (section 1), not only by the "smallest relation" sentence; and it is refused by the decided library route, `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:45` (one library, the interpreter's; "How the checker is brought to accept the library — the exclusion sites, ... — is a plan put to him step by step, not a decision to re-ask"). Keeping the rule means the checker can never accept the library's nested tower (61 errors at 26 sites, `CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:73`), so it is the library route re-asked. The designers adopted the rule to buy specialised generic overloads that the specification forbids (`justificationOfRTR.tex:76-84` against `overloading.tex:100-105`); the revival is not bound to buy them.

2. **"Drop it together with enforcing `overloading.tex:100-105`" over-states what soundness needs.** The hole is the Return Type Rule check trusting one instantiation (`OverloadingOracle.scala:88-95`). The sentence closes it, but the sentence is a restriction on every overload set, generic-beside-generic included, and its cost was left unmeasured by the worker (REPORT.md, "What this does not settle", third item). Measured here by a column-0 grep for a declaration `name[\...\](` beside `name(` in the same file (functional methods and nested declarations not counted, so a lower bound): `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/Compiled12.invariantInference.fss:52-61` (run by its `.test`) and `compiler_tests/Compiled6.ak.fss:14-15` (a bare `.fss`; whether the suite runs it was not checked); `library_tests/` 0; `LibraryBuiltin/` 0, so the compiler prelude has none; the interpreter's library `Library/Generator2.fss:52-57` (`takeleft[\T\](a: Nothing[\T\], b: Any)` beside `takeleft(a: Any, b: Any)`, and `takeright` the same); and in the interpreter's gated `tests/`, `overloadTest8.fss:33-37`, `doubledOverloading.fss:36-41`, `GeneratorNullPointer.fss:18-20`, `ArrayListQuick.fss:36-55` and `PureListQuick.fss`. Every one of these return types is `String`, `()`, `ZZ32` or the parameter-free `Any`: none mentions the generic's parameter, so none has the hole, and the sentence would refuse all of them for no soundness. This is the measured cost that makes the sentence Pavol's and not a repair worker's.

3. **The interpreter's rule is narrower than the worker reads it.** `OverloadedFunction.java:496-498` refuses a pair when a symbolic type was seen or a parameter pair is *unrelated* and nothing excludes; `walk` accepts `Library/Generator2.fss:52-57` and `tests/GeneratorNullPointer.fss:18-20`, both one-generic-one-not, both subtype-related in every position. The worker's table cell "interpreter: refused" is measured for the `Tag[\X\]` beside `Tag[\ZZ32\]` shape (`probes/walk-ProbeMIEPickCtl.txt:5-6`) and must not be generalised to every specialised overload. The error text itself says what the test is: "unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor equal) and no excluding pair is present" (`probes/probe-overload.txt:39`).

4. **Home 3 for `pick[\X\]` beside `pick` is the right home for the wrong reason.** The worker gave it home 3 so as not to pre-empt decision (b) (REPORT.md, "The three homes", item 2). An XXX file is deleted with the decision either way, as the worker itself says of the other XXX file, so that reason does not hold. The reason that holds is mechanical: a program that links and runs today cannot be an expected-failure test. In `FileTests.java:384-404`, an XXX test whose link succeeds and whose run exits 0 has `anyFails` false and `trueFailure` null, and is red today as "Missing expected failure" (`:399-402`); with `link_err_contains` set it is red as "Saw wrong failure" (`:394-397`). Home 2 has no working form for "accepted today, the specification says refuse", so the probe and the ledger row are the only home. The record should say this, not the pre-emption argument.

5. **The trade-off is not symmetric in the way the worker's table suggests.** The worker's table says "either column's pair is sound". The specification's column is sound because of the call-site instantiation model (`overloading.tex:106-108`, `trait-parameters.tex:374-379`), not because of (O) alone; the 2011 column is sound because of multiple instantiation exclusion. Whether the compiled code generator instantiates a dispatched generic overload from the call site's static arguments or by inspecting the argument's run-time type is the fact on which every sound closure short of the full sentence depends (Naden's `headOrID`, `justificationOfRTR.tex:481-494`: without the rule "we need to choose an instantiation without any means to do so"). The worker did not name this, and neither the trace nor the triage measured it. `ProbeMIEPick` shows only that a *non-generic* specialisation is chosen at run time regardless of the call site's `X = String`.

## 4. Why this is a reserved fork and not a silent specification

Rule 4 of the brief: the specification answers a divergence; a silent specification is the reason to think harder, not to stop. The specification here is not silent. On the divergence "`pick[\X\]` beside `pick`: compiled accepts, `walk` refuses" it sides with `walk` (`overloading.tex:100-105`), which is rule 4's first outcome, repair. The repair is the sentence, and the sentence is what the batch record reserved to Pavol before this rung ran (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:18`; `triage.md:113`, "(b) is Pavol's decision about the specification, not a patch: the 35, and the sentence's reach over overrides"). It was reserved because the library the route makes the standard uses shapes the sentence refuses (the triage's 35 sites; `Library/Generator2.fss:52-57` in this ruling), and `POSITIONS.md:39` makes the library's practice the standard. A judge does not lift a reservation the coordinator wrote into the record Pavol launched with "go".

The candidates short of the sentence were derived and each falls on a stop of its own:

- The interpreter's rule ported to the compiled checker (a symbolic pair needs an excluding or subtype-related position everywhere) refuses generic-beside-generic sets with overlapping unrelated domains that the sentence permits (same parameters, different domains), which is a change of semantics against what the specification does say — `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md:52`'s fork.
- The Return Type Rule quantified over every instantiation that can co-apply — the exact rule — is sound in every model, but its conservative form (hold a static parameter of the less specific declaration rigid when it occurs in the return type and the solution pins it to something other than a bare parameter of the more specific declaration) also refuses spec-valid generic-beside-generic pairs with parameter-dependent return types *unless* the code generator dispatches at the call site's instantiation. That fact is unmeasured (section 3, item 5), and reading codegen for it is a design pass, not a repair round.
- The restricted form that refuses only a non-generic specialisation beside a generic declaration whose return type depends on its parameter (the hole's exact shape; a sub-rule of the sentence, so not against the specification; accepts all the corpus sites of section 3 item 2) is sound only under the call-site model, for the same reason.

So every sound closure is the reserved sentence, or against the specification in a corner, or conditional on a fact about the code generator that no one has measured. That is the second design decision `CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:85` names, found by a probe instead of by the suite. Stop.

## 5. Rulings on the branch as it stands

- The XXX test stays. It is the home-2 tripwire for (H), shown red on the local fix. No positive test lands, because no relaxation lands.
- The record's FACTS line on the rule's provenance stands, with the two citations of section 1 added (`trait-parameters.tex:359-367`, `:383-397`).
- The record's FACTS line "relaxing `checkP` alone is unsound in every placement" stands as measured.
- The provisional ledger row (354 in the worker's numbering; the gather assigns the number) stands, with its "notes / workaround" cell corrected: strike "keep the rule on the compiled path" as a candidate, and replace "or drop it together with enforcing `overloading.tex:100-105`" with the fork of section 6.
- The note to row 97 stands as written.
- Home 3 for `pick[\X\]` beside `pick` stands, with the reason of section 3 item 4 replacing the worker's.
- The manifest consequence stands: with P stopped, L's declared 102 is the merged tree's count if L lands alone (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:67`); the 23 is not reachable in this batch.
- Nothing under `ProjectFortress/src` changed on the branch; `ProjectFortress/build` in the worktree holds the measurement build with the switch off, which the gather does not take.

## 6. What reaches Pavol

**The fork.** The compiled checker's `checkP` is the 2011–2012 team's multiple instantiation exclusion. The specification refuses it (`types-vals-vars.tex:184-189`; `trait-parameters.tex:359-367`, `:383-397`) and the library route needs it gone (61 of the 93 errors, `CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:73`). Removing it, in any placement, opens one hole: the compiled overloading checker's Return Type Rule trusts the one instantiation that the rule used to guarantee (`OverloadingOracle.scala:88-95`), and a six-line program then type-checks and dies (`probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss`; `probe-matrix.txt:67`). The question is which rule replaces the reliance.

**The candidates and their costs.**

(a) **The specification's sentence** (`overloading.tex:100-108`): overloads of a name share their static parameters; a call site instantiates them once. This is triage decision (b). Closes the hole; makes the run-time choice of instantiation moot on the checker's side.
